name: No-Boil Chicken Pasta Casserole with Artichokes and Peas

ingredients.buy: 12 oz (2 1/3 of the 5.2 oz packages), crumbled
1 lb 4 oz drained (about 2 1/3 cans), roughly chopped
2 1/3 tsp finely grated (zest of the same lemons)

writer_notes: Batch scales the 6-serving source recipe by a clean 7/3 (2 1/3x) across nearly all lines.

Chicken broth flagged: 2.5 cups source x 7/3 = 5.833 cups, but locked buy string reads 5 3/4 (5.75). Minor scale drift; left for the engine to resolve since broth is the cooking liquid for no-boil pasta.

All 13 locked ingredients are used by a step; no orphans and no invented ingredients. Sauce = cottage cheese + Boursin + garlic + lemon juice + zest + salt + broth; assembly = penne + chicken + peas + artichokes; parmesan tops; parsley garnishes.

Boursin real-world buy is 3 packages (15.6 oz) to cover the 12 oz / 2 1/3-package call; prose says buy three without promising a specific leftover, and makes no per-ounce or lasts-several-batches cost claim (no cost_lines available to name).
Macros carried as tokens {{cal}}/{{protein}} and cost as ${{cost_ps}} so they bind to the built spec. No literal dollar figure in prose except the $1/month membership line.
Band verified: 603 cal (450-800), 54.8 g protein (>=40), carbs unrestricted; chicken breast protein and penne carb source both compliant.

prose.intro_html:
Here is the trick this casserole pulls off: the pasta never touches a pot of boiling water. You lay it in dry, pour a blended cottage cheese and Boursin sauce right over the top, and the oven does the rest while the noodles quietly drink up the chicken broth. One less pot to scrub is a small win, and this build stacks fourteen of them.

It is also, without making a big deal about it, a protein workhorse. Between the chicken breast, the cottage cheese, and the parmesan, every container lands at {{protein}} grams of protein and {{cal}} calories. Artichoke hearts, peas, and a bright hit of lemon keep it from tasting like a gym supplement. This is comfort food that happens to do your macros a favor.
prose.shop_smart:
The two cheeses do the heavy lifting, so start there. Boursin comes in 5.2 ounce packages, and the build calls for 2 1/3 of them, so pick up three and you are covered with a little to spare. Cottage cheese you want a full 2 pound 5 ounce amount; any brand blends smooth once it hits the blender, so grab whatever tub is friendliest to the wallet.

Penne is the workhorse at 1 pound 12 ounces dry, and since a standard box is a pound, two boxes cover it. For the artichoke hearts, canned and drained is what you want, about 2 1/3 cans worth once you pour off the liquid. Frozen peas are the easy call and you only need 2 1/3 cups, so a small bag handles it. Grate the parmesan fresh off a wedge if you can; it melts nicer over the top than the pre-shredded stuff.
prose.make_it:
Get the oven to 400 degrees and lightly grease a 9 by 13 casserole dish. This is a fourteen serving batch, so you may be running two dishes; grease both while you are at it.

The sauce is a blender job. Drop in the cottage cheese, the crumbled Boursin, the minced garlic, the fresh lemon juice, the lemon zest, and the sea salt, and blend until smooth. Then pour in the chicken broth and blend again until it is silky and fully combined. Do not panic when it looks thin, because that thin sauce is exactly what cooks the dry pasta.

Now the dump. Lay the dry penne across the bottom, then scatter the cubed chicken breast, the peas, and the chopped artichoke hearts over it. Pour the blended sauce over everything and make sure every noodle is submerged. Cover the dish tightly with foil.

Bake covered for 40 minutes. Pull it out, take off the foil, and give it a good stir; the pasta should still be a touch undercooked at this point. Scatter the parmesan over the top and return it to the oven uncovered for another 5 to 10 minutes, bumping the heat up if you want a golden top. Let it rest at least 10 minutes so it sets, then finish with the chopped parsley and serve.
prose.portion_html:
Fourteen even containers is easier than it sounds, and the honest way is to weigh it. Weigh your empty casserole dish before you cook, or weigh the finished bake and subtract the dish, so you know the weight of the food alone. Divide that number by fourteen, and the result is your target grams per container. Scoop, weigh, adjust, and every lid closes on the same {{cal}} calories and {{protein}} grams of protein.

Eyeballing it means the first few boxes come out heaping and the last person gets sauce and regret. The scale keeps everybody honest, and it costs you about ninety seconds.
prose.cost_closing_html: Here is the part your budget actually cares about. This whole casserole breaks down to ${{cost_ps}} per serving, and for that you get {{cal}} calories and {{protein}} grams of protein in a real dinner, not a sad desk salad. Cook the batch once, eat it across the week, and that is how the number stays that small.

head.description: A no-boil dump-and-bake chicken pasta casserole with artichokes, peas, and a creamy cottage cheese and Boursin sauce. High in protein, easy on the budget, and scaled to make 14 meal-prep servings.
head.keywords: no boil chicken pasta casserole, dump and bake pasta, high protein meal prep, chicken artichoke casserole, cottage cheese pasta bake, budget meal prep dinner, penne casserole
steps: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F and lightly grease a 9x13 casserole dish.

In a blender or food processor, combine the cottage cheese, crumbled Boursin, minced garlic, fresh lemon juice, lemon zest, and sea salt, and blend until smooth. Add the chicken broth and blend again until the sauce is completely smooth and thin.

Place the dry penne in the bottom of the dish, then scatter the cubed chicken breast, peas, and chopped artichoke hearts over the top. Pour the blended sauce over everything, making sure the pasta is fully submerged.
Cover the dish tightly with foil and bake for 40 minutes. Remove the foil, stir well, top with the parmesan, and bake uncovered for another 5 to 10 minutes until golden.
Let the casserole rest for 10 minutes, then top with chopped parsley or basil and serve.
